I've been wondering about this matchup for years, considering how this matchup seems so natural. You have two long-running fantasy video game series (Zelda and Castlevania), each with a Dark Lord that continuously rises back to life over the course of ages. Even if you stick closely to canon (no Hyrule Warriors or Lords of Shadow), there is so much material to draw from.

Round 1: Ganondorf and Dracula face off one-on-one in their human forms. A duel of evil sorcerers.

Round 2: Both sides can use their "Final Form." This involves Ganondorf becoming one of his pig-like incarnations and Dracula becoming a Demon thing.

Round 3: Battle of Dark Hordes. Both Ganondorf and Dracula bring their respective minions into the battle, and fight alongside them. This includes both common enemies and bosses from the Zelda and Castlevania games. Ganondorf would get his Moblins, Darknuts, Poes, and Soldiers led by the likes of Twinrova, Phantom Ganon, and Gohma, while Dracula's legions of wild animals, animated skeletons, zombies, ghosts, and demons would be led by Death, Legion, and Mummies.

Bonus Round: Apply non-canon material to any of the above.

Please mention any thoughts you have below. I'm going to give a comment giving the outcome I'd expect for each round.

Round 1: I think that this fight would be roughly tied, with Ganondorf having the slight upper hand. Both fighters have a number of ranged magical attacks, but whereas Dracula largely focuses on Fire-based magic, Ganondorf has used Light magic fairly frequently, most famously in Ocarina of Time. This should give Ganondorf the advantage in terms of magic projectiles, and he also uses similar Light magic to passively harm foes during combat. This usually backfires when fighting Link, because Ganondorf shares this weakness, but Dracula is at a sort of elemental disadvantage.However, besides ranged spells and the ability to float in the air, Ganondorf has used a variety of swords across the Zelda series, while Dracula can be transform and teleport. Although Ganondorf gains a close-ranged advantage, Dracula stas at a distance by default, and these abilities give him a way to counter Ganondorf's elemental advantage. I'd give Ganondorf the endurance advantage at least, based on what kinds of punishment he's taken. I'd say Ganondorf wins 6/10.

Round 2: Ganon wins this round. Ganon's most common "Final Form" is that of the big pig-like sorcerer with a trident. To my knowledge, this form appeared in at least six games across multiple timelines, while no other form had multiple appearances. Dracula's "Final Form" is a touch less predictable, but will be big and demonic. Dracula's demon forms have used fire, dark, and electric magic spells, flight, strikes with his claws, and summoning darkness. All very cool, but Ganon's list of powers here is ridiculous. He has all the physical strength you'd expect from a big pig monster, and also has the intelligence and trident to take advantage of it. Ganon doesn't use much Light magic, but has plenty of Fire magic to make up for it, including the invincible Blazing Bats. Ganon also keeps lightning magic, as fired through his trident, and can create earthquakes that damage nearby foes. Also, he not only gains Dracula-level teleportation, but tosses his trident around teleporting so that he can catch it and throw it again, showing a level of teleportation skill even Dracula has trouble matching. And Ganon can fight in the Darkness just fine. Ganon wins 8/10.

Round 3: This is Dracula's strongest round. Looking back, Ganondorf and Ganon don't necessarily have as strong an army as Dracula gets. Bear in mind that many, if not most, enemies in the Zelda series are not associated with him, wheareas most Castlevania enemies are tied to Dracula. The backboe of Ganon's armies is Mobins (pig-like goblins) and variants of them. They will use spears at a range or up close, but rarely show signs of great intelligence. There are some variants though: the tiny Miniblins work well in packs; Bokoblins are small but smart enough to use a variety of weapons and use strategy; and Bulbins, a tribe from Twilight Princess that can fight mounted on speeding boars by shooting flaming and explosive arrows, are quite useful. Ganondorf also uses undead forces such as the ghostly Poes, armored Darknuts, and creepy Redeads, and these pig and undead forces are supported by Hylian soldiers controlled by Ganon's dark magic. It's a decent mixture, but only the Darknuts and Bulbins stand out as being "Elite."

Dracula's forces can be divided into four rough categories: Animals, Undead, Humanoids, and Demons. Dracula can twist wild creatures such as birds, bats, and wolves into doing his bidding. However, he doesn't actually improve their abilities, make them more of a nuisance than anything. His Undead forces include skeletal, ghostly, and zombie forces. Dracula's skeletal troops are much sturdier than, say, a Stalchild, and are actually able to use weapons such as bows, blades, and flails. Ghosts and possessed objects can often bypass defenses, though zombies are as weak as you'd expect. Some of Dracula's more humanoid allies include actually humans, including witches, mermen, and the agile hoppers. But most dangerous are his Demons, which often have the brawn and magic to serve as bosses before becoming common enemies. This combination of lesser forces has more variety and power than Ganondorf's.

Ganondorf has a similar problem considering his higher ups, bosses and mini-bosses. Some of Ganon's best include Twinrova, a twin witches with mastery of Fire and Ice magic, Phantom Ganons, replicas of Ganondorf that serve as autonomous puppets, Gohma, a giant spider with a vulnerable eye, the Helmaroc King, a giant armored bird from Wind Waker that essentially served as Ganondorf's second in command, and Armos Knights heavily armored foes that require precise shots. As a group, Ganondorf's elite forces have excellent defenses, sometimes being immune to entire categories of damage. However, they also tend to have exploitable weaknesses, some of which are easily covered by Dracula's army. Fire and projectile attacks can come from the average skeleton or witch, let alone an equal.

Dracula's bosses are generally not as impressive as Ganondorf's. They include Giant Bats, Mummies, Medusa, Legion, and Behemoth. The reason I didn't go as into depth is because compared to Ganondorf's bosses, these have less obvious strengths and weaknesses. The grotesque Legion, a floating mass of compressed corpses, can be beaten the same way as the Behemoth: repeated contact with pointy objects. The main exception though, and huge game-changer, is Death. Death is easily Dracula's best servant. In addition to simply waving his mighty scythe to wipe out waves of foes with ease, he is famous for his ability to create flying blades that appear across a wide area. Much like Dracula, he also has Dark magic attacks and teleportation. And he is able to open the gates of hell to summon more demons, Dracula's best minions. Best of all, Dracula can absorb Death in case of emergency, which heals him and grants him a last form: True Dracula. In his native series True Dracula is capable of defeating the player in seconds, with great wings capable of both speedy flight and crushing foes, summoning pillars of magic, using Death's flying blades thing, and bypassing any special defenses. This form gives Dracula the edge he needs to counter Ganon. And with the aid of a superior army, Dracula has the upper hand. Dracula wins 8/10.
